The one substantial theorem is that the Jordan unit is an ORDER UNIT (eja_exists_isSumSq_nsmul_one_sub, hence toOrderUnitSpace), and it avoids spectral theory by finite-dimensional separation: were the elements below a natural multiple of 1 not everything, Hahn-Banach would give a nonzero linear f that is ≤ 0 there, hence ≥ 0 on squares and 0 at 1, and 0 ≤ f((a+t*1)*(a+t*1)) = f(a*a) + 2t*f(a) for every real t forces f = 0. status: repaired 2026-09-04: 1046 new lines, compile exit 0 with no new warnings. Four steps. (1) POWER-ASSOCIATIVITY, eja_pow_mul_pow: one induction on i+j proving both x^i x^j = x^(i+j) and that the multiplications by x^i and x^j commute; the commuting half comes from Mathlib's two_nsmul_lie_lmul_lmul_add_add_eq_zero, the full linearisation of the Jordan identity, re-exported pointwise as eja_lin, through the relation c_p + c_q + c_r = 0 for p+q+r = N, which with the antisymmetry c_k = -c_(N-k) forces c_k = k c_1 and then N c_1 = 0. (2) Evaluation of real polynomials at x is then a MULTIPLICATIVE linear map ejaEv, so the polynomials killing x are generated by a monic minimal polynomial (eja_exists_minpoly, by division with remainder and minimal degree). (3) FORMAL REALITY FORCES THAT POLYNOMIAL TO SPLIT INTO DISTINCT LINEAR FACTORS: a monic quadratic factor with negative discriminant is a square plus a positive constant, and multiplying the minimal polynomial by the complementary factor writes 0 as a sum of two squares (eja_minpoly_split, on Mathlib's IsMonicOfDegree.eq_isMonicOfDegree_one_or_two_mul); a repeated factor makes a polynomial of smaller degree square to zero (eja_minpoly_nodup). (4) The Lagrange basis polynomials of the roots, evaluated at x, are the spectral idempotents. The POSITIVITY half needs a Euclidean structure, which the formally real definition of the class does not carry, so the file builds the trace form B x y = tr (L (x*y)) itself: it is associative because the commutator of two multiplications is a derivation (eja_der - exactly two instances of the linearised identity added, the four four-fold products cancelling by commutativity), and positive definite (ejaB_self_pos) by the spectral theorem together with the positivity of the trace of a non-zero idempotent (eja_tr_idem_pos, from the Peirce relation 2L^3 - 3L^2 + L = 0 at an idempotent and the two idempotent Peirce projections, whose traces are the ranks of their ranges). Then L p is positive semidefinite for B whenever p is idempotent, so a sum of squares pairs non-negatively with every idempotent, and that is what forces the spectral values of a sum of squares to be non-negative.
